judge_assessment.explanation: The judge is right about the count (twelve \problem bodies; the machine warning is a text-extraction artefact of numbers printed inside the items) and right about the mathematics. I recomputed all eighteen checks: 48->50, 83->80, 260->300, 418->400, 536<563, 365->370, the ascending 273/307/370, 650->700, 409<490, 472-470 = 2 and 480-472 = 8 with 472->470, the descending 481/418/184/148, the ascending 287/296/312, and all three room counts rounding to 300. Two claims do not survive. 'The manual challenge is properly supported' is true of problem 12(c) but incomplete: problem 9 also asks the child to 'say in one sentence what Mia should have compared first' and carries only a compare entry (409 < 490) with no manual entry -- the same one-sentence explanation demand, flagged in one place and not the other, and final_response.md consequently says 'One item is flagged for manual review' when two items require written reasoning. Second, 'All twelve interleaved problems are legible' does not address coverage: the directions instruct 'Write a number on each short line under the long marks', and the \nline macro draws three label rules under every number line, so problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 each print three label slots plus the result. verify.json records only the rounded result; the end and middle labels (40, 45, 50 for problem 1) exist only in the key's prose. The Quick Answers bank also prints '5. -' and '9. -' for two verified '<' relations.

strengths_to_preserve: The tie rule is stated in the directions ('If a number lands exactly on the middle mark, round to the bigger end') and then deliberately tested twice: problem 6 rounds 365 to the nearest ten and problem 8 rounds 650 to the nearest hundred, both landing exactly on the middle mark. Teaching a convention and then examining it is the right use of the interleaved format.

Problem 12 is a genuine synthesis rather than a longer exercise: 287, 296 and 312 all round to 300, so part (c) forces the student to articulate what rounding destroys -- the ordering they just produced in part (a).

Problem 10 decomposes the rounding decision into the two distances (472 is 2 past 470 and 8 short of 480) and verifies both as separate eval entries, so the 'which end is closer' reasoning is checked, not just its conclusion.

root_causes.description: Coverage is per problem id, so the number-line labelling that the directions explicitly require -- three written values per rounding problem -- is unverified, and only the final rounded value is checked.
evidence: worksheet.tex defines \nline as a blank number line drawing three short label rules under the left end, middle and right end; the directions say 'Write a number on each short line under the long marks'.
Problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 all invoke \nline; verify.json records only an estimate entry per id (50, 80, 300, 400, 370, 700, 470).
The correct labels exist only in the key's prose ('the left end is 40 and the right end is 50 ... the middle mark is at 45').

root_causes.description: An explanation prompt becomes a manual entry only if the author remembers, so the same demand is flagged in problem 12(c) and unflagged in problem 9, and the delivery summary undercounts manual items.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 9: '... then write the correct symbol, $<$ or $>$, between them and say in one sentence what Mia should have compared first.'
verify.json id 9 has a single compare entry; id 12 carries a manual entry for its one-sentence explanation.
final_response.md: '**One item is flagged for manual review, on purpose:** problem 12(c) ...'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sends relation strings through bare sympify, which raises, and returns '---', the same glyph used for manual-only rows.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '5. -' and '9. -'; every other row prints values.
verify.json ids 5 and 9 are compare/relation with expected '<', both verified.
The key body prints '536 < 563' in full, so only the bank loses it.

improvements.title: Verify the number-line labels the directions tell the student to write
improvements.proposed_change: Make SKILL.md's coverage rule slot-level and extend tests/check_layout.py to count response rules per \problem, including the three label rules \nline draws. For each rounding problem require entries for the left end, middle and right end (40, 45, 50 for problem 1) alongside the rounded result, so the model the sheet is built on is checked rather than only its conclusion.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with a \nline rounding problem whose verify.json carries only the estimate entry: tests/check_layout.py must exit non-zero naming the three uncovered label rules. Passes today (seven problems here have that shape); after the fix only the four-entry version passes.
improvements.expected_impact: The number-line model that gives this task its name becomes machine-checked, so a mislabelled midpoint in a key could not ship green.
improvements.risk: \nline is a shared macro, so every existing number-line worksheet will fail until back-filled; the counter must know which macros draw response rules and which draw decoration.

improvements.title: Flag problem 9's one-sentence explanation manual, as problem 12(c) already is
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate scanning \problem bodies for explanation cues ('say in one sentence', 'explain', 'tell how you know') that fails unless the id carries a manual entry, and derive the manual count printed in the delivery summary from verify.json so 'One item is flagged' cannot be written while two items demand sentences.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture where one problem says 'say in one sentence what Mia should have compared first' with only a compare entry and a sibling has the same prose plus a manual entry: the gate fails the first, passes the second. Fails today.
improvements.expected_impact: Accurate manual-review counts, and grading guidance attached to every explanation a teacher must read.
improvements.risk: Cue matching can over-trigger on narrative stems; scope to imperative sentences with an override.

improvements.title: Print the verified '<' for problems 5 and 9 in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt before the sympify call and typeset them with the compared 'values' ('$536 < 563$'), and emit a distinct marker for manual-only rows so a dash unambiguously means 'a human must read this'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: a compare/relation entry must render the relation, never '---', and must differ from the manual marker. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The two comparison rows on an otherwise complete bank stop reading as unchecked work.
improvements.risk: Slightly wider entries can change the bank's column count.

case_summary: Twelve genuinely interleaved problems with correct mathematics throughout -- I recomputed all eighteen checks, including both deliberate exact-midpoint cases (365 -> 370, 650 -> 700) that exercise the tie rule the directions state -- and a synthesis item where all three counts round to 300, which makes rounding's information loss the lesson rather than an aside. Three gaps behind the 32/32: the number-line labels the directions require the student to write are unverified on all seven rounding problems, so only the final answer was ever checked; problem 9's one-sentence explanation is recorded as a bare comparison while the identical demand in 12(c) is flagged manual, leaving the delivery summary's manual count one short; and the bank prints dashes for the two verified relations.
